newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel general says need to deter, not conquer Iran.
newsitem.headline: Israel general says need to deter, not conquer Iran.

text.p: Israel's deputy army chief of staff said in an interview published on Thursday the Jewish state would not conquer Iran but wanted to deter any attack.
Major-General Matan Vilnai also said Israel had to be ready for war with Syria because it had not dropped its war option, Israel's mass-circulation daily Maariv said.

Israel's Haaretz daily said Iran had recently received from North Korea a computer programme needed to produce the Nodong surface-to-surface missile which, with a 1,200-km (746-mile) range, was capable of hitting Israel.
It said Iran was helping finance North Korea's Nodong missile development.
Haaretz gave no source for the report but quoted senior diplomatic sources as saying Israel had asked the United States to raise the missile issue with North Korea.

"A situation must be created that will make Iran think twice if it is worthwhile for it to start with us," Maariv quoted Vilnai as saying. Vilnai said Israel "would not conquer Iran nor declare war on it" but had the power to deter an attack.
He said Russia was cooperating militarily with Iran.

"The cooperation is very important to the Iranians, although I suppose that over time they will build their own capability. Now they are like a baby that someone has to lead so the Russians are doing this," Vilnai said.

Israel has long worried publicly about a Russia-Iran connection. On April 13, Israel's air force chief said Iran had ground tested a missile capable of hitting the Jewish state with the help of Russian experts.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said after a visit to Moscow in March that Russian President Boris Yeltsin had assured him "ballistic missile development...was not taking place and will not take place".
Vilnai said Syrian President Hafez al-Assad had yet to rule out war with Israel as an option.
"Assad hasn't said this, so we have to stay prepared. Just because the Syrians are quiet now doesn't mean they won't move one day, and we have to prepare our response," he said.
U.S.-sponsored Israel-Syria peace talks launched in 1991 broke down more than a year ago.
